turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale. I have until twenty to five. Withdraw the zero, and then we can talk about why my son found out from his phone in the middle of class.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Kalinowski is fine. You asked for this meeting, so start with what you have, not with thanks.
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. Even the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Quite reliable." Okay. Your own procedure, section 4.3, says software results don't establish a concern by themselves. Is there a document in front of you, or is that all you have?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." So you decided first and asked questions later. Section 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Owen read it on his phone in the middle of class.
I hope you understand my position.
"I hope." Okay. Your position so far is a score from software and a zero you entered before anyone called me. I'm writing that down, and I'll ask once more: what else do you have?
